title: План саботажа на кухне  (The Kitchen Sabotage Plan)

segments.t: Watching Aleksandr spend two hours crafting a single plate just to impress Vika, Lyova, Senya, and Fedya decide to teach the cocky newcomer a lesson. They plot to desert their stations right as the evening dinner rush hits to see how the young genius handles a real crisis.
Одно блюдо за два часа сделал.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Not bad, simply good.' In Russian, the idea of 'not bad' flows naturally into 'fine' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
Одно блюдо за два часа сделал.
'He spent two hours making a single dish.' The meaning hinges on 'one' working together with 'to do' in spoken Russian.
'I would like to see him show off like that during a rush.' Notice how Russian expresses 'tried' and 'show off' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'We need to stage a kitchen rush.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'at' and finishing on 'rush'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Then we will see how fast he runs around.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'have a look' and 'then' in a few short words.
'Well then, I should get going.' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'go' in spoken Russian.
'Goodbye, Viktor Petrovich.' Notice how Russian expresses 'until' and 'Petrovich' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'There was something I wanted to ask of you.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'to ask'.
'You see, whenever you come to visit.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'understand' before landing on 'come'.
'Viktor Petrovich starts feeling much better.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Viktor' and finishing on 'better'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Is that so?' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'really' in spoken Russian.
'It would mean a lot to him.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'to him' and finishing on 'pleasant'.
'I can stop by this evening.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'can' in a few short words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Одно блюдо за два часа сделал.
